column2: Commentary
Instrument Number:

Aker Kvaerner Chemetics standard instrument number is to be used for all projects.  Instrument numbers are taken from the master instrument list for each particular technology.  The owner column is only to be filled in if by contract we must use the Owner's numbering system.  For criteria/basic engineering projects this column should be left blank.
P&ID:
The P&ID which each particular instrument is physically located.
Fluid:
The type of fluid the pressure regulator comes into contact with.  Be specific - use the fluid description given in 1-LSt-0002 Fluid Codes.
Composition:

List all major components in the fluid stream in % weight/weight.  % volume/volume can be used for gases (e.g. stack analyzer for measuring O2 in H2 or Cl2 in air).  Trace components should be specified when they potentially have an impact on materials of construction (e.g. trace Cl2 or trace hypo).
Physical Properties @ N.O.C.:
The desnity of the gas (or liquid) at normal (flowsheet) temperature, composition and pressure.
The vapour pressure of the liquid at normal (flowsheet) temperature, pressure and composition.
Flowrate:
Min. - minimum expected flow through regulator during plant operation, turndown, upset, sutdown or start-up conditions.
Norm. - flowsheet value
Max. - maxiumum expected flow through regulator during plant operation, turndown, upset, shutdown or start-up conditions.
Temperature
Min. - minimum expected temperature during plant operation, normal turndown, upset, shutdown or start-up conditions.  Consider ambient temperature.
Norm. - flowsheet value
Max. - maximum expected temperature during plant operation, upset, shutdown or start-up conditions.  Consider ambient temperature.
Note:  Maximum temperature is not the pipe or equipment design temperature.
Inlet Pressure:
Calculated line pressure at regulator inlet normal and maximum flows.
Not required for criteria/basic engineering projects.
Pressure Drop:
Calculated pressure drop across the regulator normal and maximum flows.
Not required for criteria/basic engineering projects.
Shut-off Pressure:
Maximum expected line pressure at regulator inlet.  Consider pump dead head pressure, thermal expansion and relief valve set pressure.
Not required fro criteria/basic engineering projects.
Pressure Setting:
The upstream or downstream pressure that the regulator should be set to control at.  Specify whether upstream or downshtream pressure is to be controlled.
Recommended Type:
Based on experience and cost, state the recommended type of pressure regulator (e.g. self acting/internal pilot)
Leakage Class:
Class I to III - not normally used.
Class IV - Intended for single -port and balanced single - port valves with extra tight piston seals and metal to metal seats.  Leakage rate is limited to 0.01% of rated valve capacity.

Class V - Intended for same types of valves as class IV.  The test fluid is water at 100 psig or operating pressure.  Leakage rated is limited to 0.0005 l/min of water per mm of port diameter per bar differential.

Class VI - Intended for resilient seating valves.  Test fluid is air or nitrogen.  Pressure is lesser of 50 psig or operating pressure.  Leakage limit is 0.15 to 6.75 ml per min or 2 to 45 bubbles per min. for valve sizes 1 through 8 inches.
Material of Construction
Wetted parts - recommended material(s) for all instrument parts that come into contact with fluid.  The material selection should normally be taken from the Instrument Spec. Sheet database.
Non-wetted parts - Note any special requirements such as paint, plastic, etc. required to protect against environment, spills, leakage, etc. Not required for criteria/basic engineering project.
Gasket/Seal - recommended material(s) for all gaskets, o-rings, etc. (e.g. PTFE, EPDM, Kalrez)
Operating Case Reference:
Reference plant(s) that have used same type regulator
Not required for criteria/basic engineering project.
Comments:
Any additional information that would be helpful in the selection (e.g. Model number, manufacturer, operating experience, included with packaged equipment etc.)
